title: AI ethics, safety and governance
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Think clearly about the ethical, safety and policy questions raised by AI: ethical frameworks applied to AI, fairness definitions and the impossibility results, privacy and differential privacy, transparency and explanation, accountability and documentation, safety problems such as specification gaming, robustness failures and misuse, effects on work, information and the environment, the debate about risks from advanced AI, and how AI is governed in law and practice, with the main views on contested questions presented fairly.
primary_reading: Introduction to AI Safety, Ethics, and Society by Dan Hendrycks (free online)

weeks.7: Accountability: documentation, audits and model cards
weeks.8: Safety problems: specification gaming, robustness and misuse
weeks.9: AI, work, information and the environment
weeks.10: The debate about risks from advanced AI
weeks.11: Governing AI: laws, standards and institutions

blocks.deliverable: Analyze a deployed system with two ethical frameworks.
Compute three fairness metrics for a classifier's predictions.
Add Laplace noise to a count and explain the privacy guarantee.
Week 7 midterm; write a model card for a classifier.
Write the strongest case for two opposing positions on AI risk.
Map a system's obligations under one AI law.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Impact assessment: for a supplied AI system description (such as a hiring screener or a hospital triage model), identify stakeholders and harms, compute fairness metrics on supplied prediction data, propose a privacy approach, write a model card, assess the system against one current legal framework, and write a recommendation with the strongest objection to it and your reply.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
